source.title: Random CNN Structure – Tool to Increase Generalization Ability in Deep Learning
source.authors: B. Świderski; S. Osowski; Grzegorz Gwardys; J. Kurek; M. Słowińska; Iwona Lugowska

record.file_problem: The supplied full text is readable and appears complete; it is a 2022 journal article, although the ID supplied is a 2021 preprint identifier.
record.tranche_reason: The study compares a random CNN structure with fixed-activation CNN structures and reports held-out performance. This is a different architectural intervention from the listed versions, so its findings fit none of them exactly.
record.gate_note: Tests whether random activation-branch selection changes generalization on a small natural-image dataset. The paper does not test random-label memorization, width past interpolation, CNN versus fully connected networks, optimizer or batch comparisons, dropout, magnitude-aware sharpness, or removing memorized examples. Figure 4 and Figure 5 show learning-epoch curves; the text gives final smoothed values for one run.
record.test_reason: The study cites original generalization papers but tests none of V1–V8. Its own experiments compare random activation-branch selection with fixed-activation CNNs. Held-out classification performance and training-data score margins do not establish any listed version.
record.authors_conclusion: The record broadly captures the authors' conclusion: they claim random activation-branch selection improves generalization with scarce training data and interpret it as implicit regularization. Their conclusion claims improvements across quality measures, although Table 1 shows lower specificity and precision than ReLU. Describe the actual dataset as verruca seborrhoica versus basal cell carcinoma; the paper inconsistently calls it melanoma versus non-melanoma.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses a random choice between ReLU and softplus branches at each layer and evaluates a small medical image dataset; it does not reproduce one of the listed claim-version procedures.
record.method_sensitivity: Activation/structure choice (random versus fixed ReLU or softplus) and training duration; the paper reports softplus overlearning and poorer test performance during prolonged training.

fits_no_version.finding: Across repeated experiments, random CNN achieved 91.8% accuracy and 0.971 AUC, versus 91.4% and 0.955 for ReLU and 89.9% and 0.947 for softplus. Random CNN also had higher sensitivity and F1, but lower specificity and precision than ReLU. No significance tests are reported.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Random selection between ReLU and softplus branches can improve some held-out classification measures relative to fixed activations on this 213-image dermoscopic dataset.

fits_no_version.finding: In one run's smoothed learning curves, random CNN ended at 92.3% accuracy and above 0.96 AUC; ReLU reached 90.5% and approximately 0.94, and softplus 77.5% and around 0.83. The authors describe prolonged-training overlearning for softplus.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Activation-branch selection affects held-out performance during prolonged training in this experimental setting.

fits_no_version.finding: Training-data score margins were 0.836 ± 0.109 for random CNN, 0.830 ± 0.124 for ReLU, and 0.800 ± 0.117 for softplus.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Random CNN has a slightly larger mean training-data probability margin than the fixed-activation CNNs in this experiment.

record.peer_reviewed: EURASIP Journal on Image and Video Processing (2022)
record.problems: Only 213 images from one medical classification dataset were used. The paper does not report training error, so train–test gaps cannot be calculated. The principal comparison is based on a small dataset and 10 repetitions of tenfold cross-validation; the text does not report significance tests. Some epoch-curve results are for a particular run. The reported score margin is not a direct measure of generalization gap.
record.rows_left_out: No results omitted; 27 rows are included. Figure 4 and Figure 5 curve points beyond the final smoothed values described in text are not separately transcribed.

untested.parts: No random-label fitting or natural-label versus random-label held-out comparison.
No width sweep, interpolation threshold, or test-error comparison beyond zero training error.
No fully connected comparator, local-connectivity ablation, or transferred convolutional initialization.
Only Adam is used; no optimizer or tuning-budget comparison.
Only batch size 10 is used; no batch-size or compensating-recipe comparison.
No dropout intervention or joint dropout and weight-decay removal.
No magnitude-scaled weight perturbations, measured generalization gaps, or comparative ranking of generalization measures.
No memorization-based example selection, removal, or retraining comparison.

record.verdict_notes: All rows concern the study's proposed method, its comparators, or a related margin measure; none supplies evidence for V1–V8. The reported numerical values match the supplied text. Natural-label held-out accuracy alone does not test V1, and random branch selection is not a dropout comparison.

versions.untested_parts: No random-label training or comparison of held-out accuracy for natural versus random labels.
No width sweep or comparison around the zero-training-error threshold.
All compared systems are CNNs; no fully connected image-classification comparator or local-connectivity ablation.
Only Adam is used; no optimizer comparison.
Only one mini-batch size is used; no batch-size comparison.
The study reports score margins, not magnitude-aware sharpness or a ranking of generalization gaps.
No examples are removed or retrained on.
